Subject: Deployment pathway criteria & prioritizing isolation risks

Hi Linda / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared starting point.

Call highlights (short):
- SLA needs: 99th latency target ~<300ms for typical prompt patterns; sustained peak ~200 qps with spiky bursts to 500 qps.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII in prompts, need to understand isolation & auditability.
- Options on table: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private VPC / on-prem (full isolation).

Primary customer questions you asked we should resolve before a POC:
1) How does shared (hosted) infra impact 99th/95th latency (noisy neighbor risk)?
2) Can Redwood guarantee isolation or provide SLA credits / fallbacks?
3) What data controls & audit logs exist for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
4) Cost/lead time tradeoffs for Dedicated pool vs Private deployment window.

My read / hypothesis: given the PII and strict 99th requirements you described, a Dedicated pool for the initial POC (4 weeks) is the most pragmatic path: short lead time, strong isolation guarantees (tenant-level GPU pool), and straightforward monitoring. Private on-prem makes sense later if you move to regulated production. Hosted API is viable only if you can accept soft isolation and stronger fallback policies.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll loop in Aditya and Marissa for technical confirmation on isolation guarantees and SLO language (see cc).
- Ben / Redwood to share a 1-page POC plan and MAP (attached).
- Tentative POC: Dedicated pool, 4 weeks, scope = latency verification (p95/p99), request throughput, and verification of audit logs.

Please reply with any corrections and indicate whether you prefer Dedicated POC or want pricing for Hosted + stricter routing (multi-region fallback) as a comparison. Happy to hop on a short follow-up.

Best,

Ben / Marissa — answering inline / short: 

1) Historical p99 behavior on Hosted multi-tenant clusters:
- Typical p50/p95/p99 for text-gen workloads we serve (short-medium prompts): ~45ms / 120-180ms / 260-420ms depending on model and sequence length.
- We track p99 variance and, on shared clusters, bursts caused by large batch jobs (long context, model warm-ups) have pushed p99 up to ~700-900ms on rare occasions. Those are outliers and we have automatic fallback routing to alternate model variants when detected. We can share anonymized time-series for similar customer workloads in the next 48 hours.

2) Isolation semantics for Dedicated pools:
- Dedicated pools = tenant-dedicated GPU capacity (no other customers colocated on the same pool). This provides strong isolation for noisy-neighbor risk (we still share underlying host OS tooling, but no cross-tenant model execution).
- We can commit to routing, per-tenant autoscaling rules, and reserved capacity for the pool, which keeps p99 behavior predictable. We typically tie an SLA to capacity commits (we'll draft language).

3) Lead time to provision Dedicated pool (200 qps baseline):
- Typical lead time: 5-10 business days if capacity is available in your target region. If we need to stand up new hardware / region-specific resources, it can take longer (3-4 weeks) — we'll confirm on a case-by-case basis.

4) Audit logs & SOC2 artifacts:
- We can provide SOC2 excerpt and sample audit logs for POC (request/response metadata, ingestion events, and access logs) — redacted as needed. Full production compliance (long-term retention / KMS integration) is part of Dedicated/Private contracts.

Suggested next step (technical):
- Short technical kickoff (30 min) with your infra/security team + our infra eng (I can join) to align on logs, scrubbed data set for POC, and routing rules.
- For the POC, Dedicated is recommended to minimize risk to your p99. Hosted could be used only with tighter routing controls and acceptance of occasional elevated p99 tail.

I'll attach a short artifact with anonymized p99 time-series for reference — sending now.

Cheers,
Aditya
